tagline: A railroad town with the Uintas ahead.
intro: South from Evanston, WYO 150 is the Wyoming end of the Mirror Lake road, about twenty minutes of driving before the byway carries on into Utah toward Kamas. Ahead are the Uinta Mountains, the only major range in the country laid out east to west.

Evanston began in 1868 as a divisional point on the transcontinental railroad, and for a moment it looked like another end-of-track town. The railroad moved the end of the line west to Wahsatch, and the town went with it. The headquarters came back the next June, and an 1871 machine shop and roundhouse gave Evanston a longevity many railroad towns lacked.

moments.title: Evanston
moments.text: Restored railroad buildings, a roundhouse among them, stand downtown in a town that once moved twelve miles west in three days and then came back.

moments.title: Uinta Mountain view
moments.text: Southbound, the Wyoming section opens on a panoramic view of the Uintas before the road continues into Utah.
